fixes.description: VerifyAsync caught only ArgumentException around IFingerprintProvider.ExtractTemplateAsync, so any other provider/vendor failure (device timeout, vendor-specific exception, an internal provider-side cancellation unrelated to the caller's own token) escaped uncaught and no FingerprintVerificationRecord was ever written, violating AC03's requirement that extraction failure is always recorded as the distinct AcquisitionFailed outcome.
fixes.fix: FingerprintVerificationService.VerifyAsync now catches every exception the provider call can raise around ExtractTemplateAsync and records AcquisitionFailed, with one carve-out: an OperationCanceledException that correlates to the caller's own passed-in CancellationToken (cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested) still propagates instead of being recorded, since a genuine caller cancellation means nothing about that attempt was ever decided.
fixes.regression_tests: tests/features/bio-bio-004/FingerprintVerificationAcquisitionFailureTests.cs - reproduces InvalidOperationException, TimeoutException, a vendor-specific exception type (FormatException), a provider-internal OperationCanceledException unrelated to the caller's token (all recorded AcquisitionFailed), and the caller-cancellation carve-out (propagates, writes no record).

summary: Implements BIO-BIO-004 (1:1 fingerprint verification against a claimed identity), reusing BIO-BIO-001's own IBiometricTemplateStore/IFingerprintProvider/IBiometricMatcher seams directly rather than re-deriving an equivalent comparison pipeline. AC01: FingerprintVerificationService.VerifyAsync resolves the claimed identity's authorised reference via IBiometricTemplateStore.GetTemplatesAsync(tenantId, personId, Fingerprint) - always the single newest enrolled template, never a 1:N search; an empty result throws FingerprintVerificationException.NoAuthorisedReference (a precondition failure, not a routine outcome). BIO-BIO-002 is the story's declared dependency but is NOT referenced directly: its own IFingerprintEnrolmentRepository/FingerprintEnrolmentService are internal, Singleton-registered, and expose no query-by-claimed-identity at all (only get-by-session-id), and captured templates live embedded in its own session aggregate, never published to BIO-BIO-001's shared store - reaching into BIO-BIO-002's owned paths to add such a query is out of this story's write scope (governance/feature-path-ownership.json), so this story verifies against IBiometricTemplateStore instead, the same seam BiometricService.EnrollAsync/VerifyAsync already define for this exact purpose, and documents the gap explicitly (see docs/features/bio-bio-004/README.md). AC02: every VerifyAsync call persists exactly one FingerprintVerificationRecord (Score/MatcherId/ProviderId/ProviderVersion/ComparisonOutcome/AccessDecision) via the internal IFingerprintVerificationRecordStore, regardless of outcome. AC03: BiometricComparisonOutcome is a closed three-member enum (Matched/NotMatched/AcquisitionFailed); after the round-1 fix, ANY exception from IFingerprintProvider.ExtractTemplateAsync (not only ArgumentException) is caught and recorded as AcquisitionFailed rather than propagating, except a genuine caller cancellation - distinct from a comparison that ran and scored zero (NotMatched). Both are routine, recorded outcomes, never thrown exceptions (AC01's missing-reference precondition is the only exception path, mirroring BIO-BIO-003's SourcePhotoNotFound treatment). AC04: Domain/IIdentityStatusGateway.cs is this story's own narrow, read-only seam onto BIO-IDN-001's PersonService (no ProjectReference - PersonService is Scoped/tenant-scoped, the same reasoning BIO-BIO-003 documents for its own upstream dependency); it is consulted only when the biometric comparison itself already matched, and IdentityStatus.Suspended/.Revoked downgrades what would otherwise be AccessDecision.Allow into .Deny with an explicit reason, while ComparisonOutcome.Matched is still recorded - a suspended/revoked identity's fingerprint match is visible to a security reviewer without ever having been capable of granting access. Repository and service are internal, gated by an explicit InternalsVisibleTo seam (BIO-IDN-001-QA-01 governance shape, mirrored from BIO-BIO-002/003).
